title: When a stock runs empty
hook: A toy stock loses more than it gains. Can repeated subtraction make the stock negative?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Distinguish depleted stock from an unmet request when a fixed-flow calculation reaches its zero boundary.

misconception: A fixed outflow can keep reducing a physical stock below zero.
objective: Distinguish depleted stock from an unmet request when a fixed-flow calculation reaches its zero boundary.

claims.text: Original stipulated feedback model: A inputs [10, 2, 6, 3] yield 0; B inputs [10, 2, 4, 3] yield 4. Prediction correct option 4. A ends at {A}; B at {B}. A would subtract twelve from ten, but the stock floor clips the final step at zero; B removes only six. Fixed flows with a zero floor only; unmet outflow is not recorded as negative physical stock.
claims.source: Original lesson construction; EDD-010 formula ; exact independent Python arithmetic recomputation recorded in answerCheck; no book dataset or measured human response.

claims.text: A toy stock starts at 5, gains 1 and is asked to release 4 per round for three rounds. Physical stock remaining? The rule max(0, stock + 1 − 4) reaches zero and stays there; unmet requests are not negative physical stock.
